elements.element: The licence grant extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly grants the internal-use licence to “Corio, its affiliates.”

elements.element: The licence grant extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly grants the internal-use licence to “its contractors acting on Corio's behalf.”

elements.element: Every fully paid-up licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The Section 2.2 licence is expressly both “fully paid up” and “perpetual.”

elements.element: Every fully paid-up licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The Section 2.2 licence is expressly both “fully paid up” and “irrevocable.”

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence is present in the supplied provisions: Section 2.1 grants a perpetual licence, and Section 2.2 grants a fully paid-up perpetual licence. The condition is therefore demonstrably absent from the provided clauses.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only if the material breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence is present in the supplied provisions, so the cure-condition requirement is not triggered.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 remain nontransferable except under Section 14.1. That section permits only specified M&A-related assignments without consent and requires consent when the transaction involves the other party's direct competitor; it does not provide general transferability to successors.

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates upon written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 gives Corio's affiliates automatic coverage without requiring notice, which is broader than coverage conditioned on written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 generally permits assignment in connection with a merger or acquisition, but requires the other party's consent if the transaction involves its direct competitor. Thus transfer to an M&A successor is not assured in all such transactions.

result.reason: The redline operatively adds affiliates, contractors, and irrevocability to the fully paid-up internal-use licence, while the supplied clauses contain no subscription licence. However, it leaves the assignment provision unchanged, including the consent requirement for M&A transactions involving a direct competitor. Accordingly, neither the preferred general successor-transfer right nor the fallback M&A-successor right is fully achieved. The changes otherwise preserve the existing licence restrictions and commercial structure.
